- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid undershooting.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 2–4% in those periods.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.44) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term upside; cap forecast at 1–3% above recent high.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.44) and price is volatile, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; smooth forecast toward recent 5-day average.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline after forecast peak, model often fails to anticipate downward momentum; reduce forecast by 3–5% in first 3–5 days post-peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate downward trends when sentiment is negative; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment <0.20.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for low sentiment-induced weakness.
